THE REWARDS PROGRAMME

Wedding credit programme terms

Earn $1,000 in wedding credits for every complete $10,000 of money paid through WedSparks. Use those credits on supplier payments through WedSparks. Credit-funded amounts do not earn additional credits.

Prepared for review · 18 October 2026 · Not yet effective. Business identity, contact details and operational rules require confirmation.

1. Scope and status2. Qualifying payments3. Milestones and examples4. Account and currency5. Availability and redemption6. Cancellations and refund adjustments7. Rights and programme changes8. Errors, misuse and support

1. Scope and status

These terms describe the intended WedSparks wedding credit programme and should be read with the Platform Terms and cancellation policy. Review draft dated 18 October 2026. Before publication, confirm the legal operator, currency, operational ledger and redemption workflow, eligible payments, refund treatment and support route.

The central programme promise is $1,000 in credits for each complete $10,000 of qualifying money paid through the WedSparks payment function. Credits are a restricted benefit for platform supplier payments. They are not a cash withdrawal, bank balance, investment return or interest payment.

2. Qualifying payments

Only money successfully paid through WedSparks towards eligible supplier invoices counts towards a milestone. A pending, failed or merely authorised payment is not treated as settled money. Recording an expense, uploading an outside receipt or marking an invoice paid manually does not make an outside payment eligible.

Amounts covered by credits do not earn more credits. The system must distinguish money paid from credits applied so the same benefit is not counted repeatedly. Any excluded transaction types must be clearly disclosed before payment rather than introduced after a couple relies on the offer.

3. Milestones and examples

Milestones are based on complete increments of $10,000 of qualifying money paid. For example, $9,000 earns no completed milestone; $10,000 earns $1,000 in credits; $25,000 earns $2,000, with the remaining $5,000 progressing towards the next milestone.

If you pay $50,000 of your own money through WedSparks, you can earn $5,000 in credits, giving $55,000 of combined purchasing power for eligible platform supplier payments. This is not $5,000 cash returned to your bank. If you later pay an invoice using those credits, that credit-funded portion does not progress the next milestone.

4. Account and currency

Credits should be recorded against the relevant couple wedding account with a visible record of earning, use and adjustment. Keep account access secure and report a balance you believe is wrong. A displayed public calculator is an illustration, not proof that a particular account has earned a balance.

Current public examples are in Australian dollars. Before offering the programme for New Zealand dollar payments or mixed currencies, publish the applicable earning currency and any conversion method. This draft does not promise exchange parity, transfer between unrelated accounts, sale of credits or pooling across different weddings.

5. Availability and redemption

Use available credits through the WedSparks payment function against eligible supplier invoices. Review the amount of credits applied and any remaining money payment before confirming checkout. Credits cannot be withdrawn as cash or redeemed by sending a supplier an outside payment.

The launch rules must state when a completed payment becomes available for earning, whether partial redemption is supported, and how an insufficient balance or a payment reversal is displayed. Do not promise a redemption path or supplier settlement arrangement that has not been implemented and verified.

6. Cancellations and refund adjustments

A refunded qualifying payment may reduce the money counted towards milestones and require an adjustment to credits earned from it. The account should show the original payment, refund and associated adjustment clearly. A refund must not result in both a retained promotional benefit and duplicate repayment of the same value.

Where an invoice used both money and credits, the refund calculation should identify each component and apply a disclosed, fair method. Before launch, settle what happens if credits earned from a later-refunded payment have already been spent. This draft does not authorise an automatic bank debit, penalty or undisclosed debt to recover a negative promotional balance.

7. Rights and programme changes

Credits are not a substitute for a money refund where one is required by law. Consumer rights relating to the supplier service and WedSparks’ own services continue to apply. Any advertising about earning must be consistent with actual eligibility and redemption rules.

No expiry period is specified by this draft. Any expiry, cap or material limitation must be expressly settled and prominently disclosed before a couple earns affected credits. Programme changes should have reasonable notice where required and fair treatment for validly accrued benefits; a broad right to erase balances without reason is not adopted here.

8. Errors, misuse and support

If you believe a balance is wrong, keep the invoice and payment reference and explain the amount in question through the support route to be published. Relevant records should be reviewed and an explanation supplied. Do not provide passwords or full card details in a credit enquiry.

Fraudulent transactions or deliberate duplicate earning may be investigated and affected benefits restricted proportionately. An account holder should have a reasonable opportunity to challenge an adjustment, except where a lawful investigation requires otherwise. Ordinary mistakes should be corrected transparently rather than treated automatically as fraud.
